messages:
elaine: Quick follow-up from the offload RFC — proposal to streamline the commit path for host-staged pages. TL;DR: keep a tiny pinned fast-path for short-lived tensors (<8MB / <50ms lifetime) and switch larger/stable buffers to an epoched host-staging commit that defers DMA until either a threshold or end-of-inference. This should reduce GPU fragmentation without increasing tail-latency for the common short requests.

kenji: sounds sensible. how do we detect "short-lived" reliably? we risk misclassifying warm-up allocations.

elaine: good point. plan is to use a moving-window lifetime estimator + hot-score counter per allocation (cheap sampling). default thresholds: 8MB and 50ms, both tunable per-tenant. we fall back to pinned if estimator is uncertain.

sanjay: how does this interact with kv-cache reuse? if a token stream reuses the same slab repeatedly we don't want it bouncing between host and pinned.

elaine: for KV-like slabs we pin once we observe repeated accesses > 3 within window. essentially treat high reuse as a separate policy: mark as "sticky-pinned".

maya: concern: staged commit defers DMA — what about OOM spikes mid-inference if host memory is exhausted? need an ordering/priority for commits and a fast fallback to eager pin.

elaine: agreed. proposal includes: 1) per-tenant host budget + watermark. 2) commit queue that prioritizes oldest in-flight requests. 3) an emergency eager-pin path when host budget below critical threshold.

chris: can we quantify perf impact? guessing worst-case extra latency is DMA time for large tensors when they finally commit, but common path stays low-latency. i can prototype a microbenchmark.

kenji: also consider fragmentation: by batching commits we might coalesce DMA into contiguous ranges -> less fragmentation on GPU allocator. but that complicates tracking.

elaine: yep batching is explicit goal. batching window default 20ms or 16KB alignment boundary; we'll add a coalesce step in commit worker. pseudo-config: 
```
offload: {
  pinned_threshold_bytes: 8388608,
  pinned_threshold_ms: 50,
  commit_batch_ms: 20,
  reuse_hits_for_sticky: 3,
  tenant_host_budget_bytes: 1e9
}
```

sanjay: telemetry we need: classification accuracy (how often we flip strategy), staged-commit queue latency, emergency-eager fallbacks, and fragmentation delta pre/post. also track per-tenant failed-commit rates.

maya: +1. add a tiny synthetic test to our CI perf harness that toggles load patterns (tiny chat vs long contexts) so we don't regress.

deploy-bot: CI: perf harness job queued (#gpu-offload-proto).

chris: i'll do the prototype and add metrics to the tracepoint events. question: should the allocator expose a "commit intent" handle so commit worker can merge adjacent pages?

elaine: i'd prefer a small opaque intent object returned at free-time so commit worker can see adjacency hints but not couple to allocator internals. simple API: `commit_intent = allocator.reserve_commit_range(ptr, len)` then worker calls `allocator.commit_range(commit_intent)`. keeps ABI stable.

kenji: that works. also thinking of adding a cheap checksum for coalescing identical free blocks across slabs — might help on multi-tenant noisy patterns.

sanjay: timeline? we should align with the next runtime release window. prototype -> perf run -> RFC update. estimate 2 weeks prototype, 1 week perf runs, then RFC revision.

elaine: ok plan: chris prototype + traces (2w), kenji help with allocator intent API (1w), maya adds CI harness toggle, sanjay config telemetry. i'll update the RFC doc with decisions and knob defaults.

maya: noted. i'll author the CI test and add a short runbook for emergency eager-pin config.

chris: starting WIP branch now, will ping when initial traces are ready.

elaine: thanks all. i'll create the RFC follow-up PR and tag reviewers. :thumbsup:
